subject: Clarify geofence activation window, transient cross-border processing & subprocessor roster
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataOps Team <datasvc@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Geofence activation window and transient cross-border processing question

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Acme found Redwood's regional pinning promising. Before we move forward with procurement, two quick items for legal/ops to confirm: 

1) Activation window: Our security team requires a committed activation timetable — we need confirmation you can have EU pinning (for our EU tenant) enabled within 30 days of contract signature. Is that achievable and what are the operational steps?

2) Transient cross-border processing: We understand temporary cross-region hops (for cold backup replication / scheduled snapshots) are possible. Please confirm the maximum window Redwood permits for transient processing without explicit case-by-case approvals (e.g., 48 hours, 72 hours?), and whether those windows are logged/auditable.

3) Subprocessors: Please provide the current subprocessor roster (CSV preferred) and flag any planned additions in the next 60 days. Our procurement team is trying to map vendor overlaps.

If it helps, loop in legal — Olivia Reed is our external counsel (cc'd). We want to avoid surprises in the DPA addendum.

Appreciate a short reply with the timeline and a roster stub we can attach to our internal review.

Best,
Lena
Lena Park 
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Acme Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geofence activation window and transient cross-border processing question

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I’ll attach the roster and proposed DPA addendum: 

- EU activation timeframe: We can commit to enabling EU region pinning for a customer tenant within 30 days of execution in typical cases. The steps: scheduling a provisioning window with ops (1–3 business days), provisioning dedicated region affinity, run smoke tests, and then apply routing policy. For high-compliance customers we add an ops playbook and validation checklist; Laura from Ops will coordinate scheduling.

- Transient cross-border window: Our standard policy allows up to 72 hours of transient cross-region processing for operational reasons (backups, replication). All transient hops are recorded in the audit logs (timestamped event with reason code) and surfaced through the Console telemetry. If a customer requires a tighter limit (e.g., 48 hours) we can bake that into the DPA addendum as a contractual limit.

- Subprocessors: attaching the current roster (CSV) with planned activations flagged. We’ll also include a short change-notice SLA in the addendum.

Next steps: I’m attaching a draft addendum (PDF) that mirrors what we discussed — it includes a 30-day EU activation commitment, a 48-hour transient hop option (if you prefer) and a subprocessor change-notice clause. Laura / Kimberly — can you confirm operational feasibility of the 30-day window and whether we should offer a 48h or 72h default in the template? I’ll then send the signed-ready DocuSign link once legal confirms language.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Fwd: Geofence activation window and transient cross-border processing question

Laura / Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding Acme's ask and my draft addendum. Key asks for legal/ops: 

- Ops: can you confirm the 30-business-day (calendar 30-day) activation commitment steps and the blackout windows we’d need? Any constraints on provisioning multiple tenants in parallel?

- Ops: confirm whether we should default to 72h for transient hops and only shorten to 48h when contractually required, or proactively offer 48h to reduce friction.

- Legal: please review the DPA addendum page 2–3 (clauses 4.2–4.5) — I added a subprocessor change-notice (14 days) and an audit/event telemetry commitment. Are these acceptable or need redlines?

Quick internal notes: 
- If we offer 48h by default we increase operational review overhead but might close Acme faster.
- If we keep 72h as default, we must ensure the Console UI exposes per-tenant transient-hop windows so customers can request 48h via the contract.

Marissa — can you flag any commercial impacts on the quote if we shorten to 48h? I can include a small premium for the shorter SLA if required.

Thanks,
Marcus
